clue.text: Highly decorated troops rejected non-fighter repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us the abbreviation for non-fighter is written a second time straight after
rejected suggests sending back, so the word for troops is turned round

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword term for troops
a CO is a conscientious objector, who refuses to fight

explanation.surface: A soldier spurns, again and again, a man who will not fight, and is somehow highly decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly decorated' looks like military medals, but it is the definition of an ornate artistic style. CO, a conscientious objector, is the non-fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the eighteenth-century style of lavish, florid ornament, so anything rococo is elaborately ornamented.

clue.text: Managed OK with cracker — cut another bakery item

indicators.note: managed suggests being handled or worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
cut means the final letter of cracker is chopped off

explanation.surface: Someone coped with a cracker and then sliced another baked treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims CRACKER to CRACKE, and 'Managed' rearranges it with OK. 'Cracker' wants to be the bakery item but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock cake is a small rough-surfaced fruit bun, a type of baked good like a cracker.

clue.text: John cheers oratorio

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet
cheers and ta-ta are both casual ways of saying goodbye

explanation.surface: A man named John applauds an oratorio.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a sung choral work with soloists, close kin to an oratorio, so one stands loosely for the other.

clue.text: Mint tea without sugar, the ultimate posh drink

parts.note: to mint money is to coin it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so tea surrounds the letter
the ultimate means the final letter of sugar is taken

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, hence posh

explanation.surface: Mint tea taken unsweetened, followed by the ultimate refined drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ultimate' gives R, the last letter of sugar, which 'without' (meaning outside) puts inside TEA. 'Mint tea' reads as one drink but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur, an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: So to speak Italian in response, knight wanted guide's backing

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for Italian inside the shortened word for a reply
wanted in the sense of lacking: the chess knight's letter is missing

parts.note: a response is an answer
N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: backing means the rear end, so only the final letter of guide's is used

explanation.surface: An Italian replies, after the knight goes missing, by having a guide turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted' means lacking, so N leaves ASWER; 'in' houses IT, and 'backing' is the rear end of guide's, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms flagging that the speaker's words are figurative rather than literal.

clue.text: Actor's reportedly regal house, rural one on river

indicators.note: reportedly means a word is spoken, giving a name of the same sound

parts.note: the Stuarts were a royal house that ruled Britain from 1603 to 1714
a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: An actor's grand country house reputedly sits by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. Stewart Granger was a British film star of the 1940s and 50s.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewart Granger was the screen name of a British film actor, star of King Solomon's Mines.

clue.text: Anita up escarpment welcomes shade

indicators.note: welcomes means the phrase holds the answer inside its letters

explanation.surface: Anita walks up a cliff and is glad of some shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Taupe is a brownish-grey colour, and a colour can be called a shade.

clue.text: Eastern mate defends daughter, a spiky thing

indicators.note: defends means the friend word surrounds the letter for daughter

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate)

explanation.surface: An Eastern friend protects his daughter from something spiky.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, shortened to china.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is the spiny anteater of Australia and New Guinea, covered in quills.

clue.text: Windows once put in Kerry's place, perish

indicators.note: put in places the old operating system's name inside the country

parts.note: County Kerry is in Ireland, Eire
XP was a Microsoft Windows version from 2001

explanation.surface: An old computer is installed in a Kerry home and promptly dies.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerry is a county in the south-west of the Republic of Ireland, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire is to die, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Footwear of sibling changing hands before American race and training run

indicators.note: before places the altered sibling first
changing hands means right becomes left, so one R becomes L

parts.note: a brother is a sibling
the Cree are a Native American people
PE, physical education, is training
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A brother's shoes swap hands before an American race and a training run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' swaps the final R (right) of BROTHER for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Brothel creepers are thick crepe-soled suede shoes, popular with 1950s Teddy boys.

clue.text: Warden back in charge getting work unit into shape

indicators.note: getting, paired with into, signals that pieces go inside the shape word
into, after getting, places the reversed abbreviation and the unit inside the shape word

parts.note: a cone is a geometric shape

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A warden returns to command and whips a work unit into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the abbreviation for in charge round, and 'getting into' puts it with the work unit inside the shape. Physics supplies the erg.
explanation.definitionFit: A concierge is a doorkeeper or caretaker of a building, so the job matches a warden's.

clue.text: Local one in square

parts.note: 'un is the dialect or local form of one, as in a good 'un
in means fashionable, which is hip

explanation.surface: A local resident sits in the village square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' is the definition in its slang sense of old-fashioned, the opposite of hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Square is slang for dull and conventional, someone unfashionable, the opposite of trendy.

clue.text: Flier left in jacket: latest offerings from Balti restaurant

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left inside the garment

parts.note: a coat is a jacket

indicators.note: latest picks the final letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: A flier leaves in his jacket after the last dishes from a Balti house.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small bird, and any bird is a flier in crossword terms.

clue.text: Wine tipped over on last word, needing Tippex?

indicators.note: on places one piece after the other in this down-the-page reading

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer

indicators.note: tipped over means the wine word is turned round

parts.note: red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: Someone spills red wine over the last word of a document and needs correction fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped over' reverses the wine. Tippex is a British brand of correction fluid, so whoever reaches for it is correcting text.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who changes written text is an amender, and correction fluid is one tool for such edits.

clue.text: Just over ten kilometres before ecclesiastical section

indicators.note: before puts the abbreviation ahead of the church part

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for kilometres
the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A runner covers just over ten kilometres before reaching part of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just over ten' looks like distance, but in a pack of cards the knave (jack) ranks immediately above the ten.
explanation.definitionFit: In playing cards the jack, also called knave, comes directly above the ten in rank.

clue.text: Hold-up by accessory? This might boost porridge dished out

definitions.text: This might boost porridge dished out

indicators.note: by places the two pieces side by side

parts.note: an accessory is something extra
a traffic hold-up is a jam

explanation.surface: A delay caused by an accomplice, while porridge is served in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, which colours the surface; the definition just means more fruit preserve on a bowl of oats.
explanation.definitionFit: A further dollop of preserve is a common way to sweeten and enrich a serving of oats.

clue.text: Something vegetarian from Korea, unusually involving shrimp

indicators.note: involving means the jumbled letters enclose the small person
unusually signals the letters of Korea are arranged in an odd way

parts.note: a shrimp or a titch (here spelt tich) is a very small person

explanation.surface: A vegetarian dish from Korea surprisingly includes shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' gives AROKE from the country's letters; 'involving' wraps it round the small person. 'shrimp' is a person here, not seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: The artichoke is a vegetable, so it suits a meat-free diet.

clue.text: Pop voice hosting jolly TV series

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, dad

indicators.note: hosting means the voice word contains the marine

parts.note: to voice is to say
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: Father speaks on a cheerful television show.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic BBC sitcom about the Home Guard in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad's Army is a British comedy programme broadcast by the BBC from 1968 to 1977.

clue.text: Polish guards behave adversely investigating vehicle

indicators.note: guards means the polishing word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to scour is to polish by scrubbing

indicators.note: adversely suggests going against, so the word is turned back

parts.note: to act is to behave

explanation.surface: Polish security staff misbehave while examining a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adversely' gives TCA, which 'guards' puts inside the polishing word. 'Polish' is not a nationality here.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout car is a light armoured military car used for reconnaissance.

clue.text: Artist's base unknown in French resort virtually

indicators.note: in puts the two letters inside the shortened town
virtually means almost all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Cannes is a resort on the French Riviera
e is the base of natural logarithms
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: An artist's place, unknown, is in a French resort, or nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' drops S from CANNES; 'in' puts EZ inside. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Cezanne was a French Post-Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Swimmer regularly at sea (Torbay)

indicators.note: regularly picks every second letter of the following words

explanation.surface: A swimmer is often out in the sea off Torbay.
explanation.walkthrough: Torbay is a stretch of the Devon coast in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The tetra is a small tropical fish, and a fish is a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Playwright calling for lawyer before start of dispute

indicators.note: before places the profession ahead of the letter

parts.note: the bar is the profession of a barrister, a lawyer's calling

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of dispute

explanation.surface: A playwright called a lawyer before the argument began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling' is a vocation, not a phone call. The Bard is Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard, short for the Bard of Avon, is a nickname for Shakespeare.

clue.text: Leon is here to stay in Ireland, Liam's heartland

indicators.note: in puts the verb inside the abbreviation

parts.note: to be is to remain, to stay

indicators.note: heartland means the central letters of Liam

explanation.surface: Leon decides to stay on in Ireland, in Liam's home region.
explanation.walkthrough: Leon is not a man but the Spanish city and region, which lies on the peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon is a city of north-west Spain, on the peninsula shared with Portugal.

clue.text: Busy worker holds quiz on cruise as deck entertainment?

indicators.note: holds means the insect contains the jumbled letters

parts.note: the bee is the proverbial busy worker

indicators.note: on cruise suggests letters drifting about, so quiz is rearranged

explanation.surface: A busy crew member runs a quiz for passengers on a cruise ship deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on cruise' scrambles the quiz letters to ZIQU, and 'holds' puts them in the insect. 'deck' means a pack of cards, not a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Bezique is a card game for two players, so it is amusement played with a pack of cards.

clue.text: Quantity of beer drunk? Time for last of soft cheese

indicators.note: for last of means the letter replaces the final letter of the cheese

parts.note: quark is a soft curd cheese

explanation.surface: Someone drinks beer and then wants soft cheese at closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time for last of' swaps the final K of QUARK for T.
explanation.definitionFit: A quart is two pints, a sizeable amount of ale one might down in a session.

clue.text: Core muscle, with miles gone, stretched by character in Marathon

indicators.note: by sets the Greek letter next to the jumbled letters

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, apt as Marathon is in Greece

indicators.note: stretched suggests pulled out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
with, joined to gone, frames the deletion of the abbreviation
gone means removed, so the abbreviation for miles is taken out of muscle

explanation.surface: A runner's core muscles are stretched over many miles of a marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with ... gone' leaves USCLE, which 'stretched' rearranges to CLEUS. Marathon is a Greek town, hence a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central part of something, its heart or centre.

clue.text: Golf club filling in trap

definitions.meaning: the ..., the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, governs golf
the letters in the middle of the word trap are ...

explanation.surface: A golfer's club gets stuck in the sand trap.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters of TRAP are R and A, which is exactly how the club's name is said.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews is universally known by its initials.

clue.text: Reptile's fear understood when picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: fear is terror and understood is saw, as in I saw what you meant

explanation.surface: A reptile's fear is grasped once someone notices it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay; the P is silent, so TERROR SAW said aloud matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Pterosaurs were the flying reptiles of the dinosaur era.

clue.text: Opening mimic about to admit loveless tour

parts.note: to ape is to mimic

indicators.note: to admit means the word for about takes in the shortened tour

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, so the O is removed

explanation.surface: An impressionist prepares to welcome a tour stripped of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops O, love being a zero score in tennis, leaving TUR; 'to admit' puts that inside the word for about.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a hole or gap, such as the opening in a camera lens.

clue.text: Sat maybe on call, peak time

indicators.note: on places one piece next to the other

parts.note: hey is a call to attract attention
Sat, short for Saturday, is an example of a day

explanation.surface: Someone sat on call at the busiest time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat' looks like the past tense of sit but is the abbreviation for Saturday.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's heyday is the period of their greatest success or vigour, their prime.
